package_info.why_malicious: FTCode is a ransomware campaign distributed via malicious Word documents containing embedded macros. These macros execute PowerShell commands that download and run ransomware, encrypting user files and demanding payment. The entire delivery chain is designed to compromise the victim's system and extort money.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on document open with macros enabled)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objShell As Object
  Set objShell = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  objShell.Run "powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command [malicious PowerShell command]"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open, the macro executes a hidden PowerShell command that downloads and runs additional malicious code, leading to ransomware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that launch PowerShell with bypassed execution policy and hidden windows are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal document macros should not launch system-level scripts or download executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation may use macros to run scripts, but never to download and execute untrusted code.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell command downloads and executes a remote script, which is the FTCode ransomware payload, leading to file encryption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote scripts is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PowerShell usage should not fetch and execute code from untrusted external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use similar commands for internal automation, but never from untrusted domains.

attack_chain.action: Victim opens malicious Word document and enables macros.
Macro launches PowerShell with execution policy bypassed and hidden window.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell downloads and executes ransomware payload.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell downloads and executes FTCode ransomware from remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment.

behavioral_signatures: Office macros launching PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass
PowerShell downloading and executing code from external domains
Hidden PowerShell windows triggered by document macros
file_indicators: Word documents with embedded AutoOpen macros
Presence of suspicious macro code invoking Wscript.Shell
network_indicators: HTTP requests to known FTCode C2 domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com/ftcode.ps1)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that contain macros invoking Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell, especially with ExecutionPolicy Bypass and WindowStyle Hidden. Detect PowerShell processes that download and execute scripts from external domains. Flag documents with AutoOpen macros that trigger system-level commands. Correlate with network traffic to known FTCode C2 infrastructure.
